title: UPDATED 5/25 - Free App Only Gives Details Of Current Day, So FAR Less Useful than Bedore
body: Update—Since they changed the basic (free) version, I don’t use it much anymore. Future days are forecast-limited to morning/afternoon/night, so basically useless. And I’m not paying $25/year for something I can pretty much get for free (NOAA, AccuWeather, Weather underground and many, many more). I think all previous reviews should be wiped clean when there’s this much of a change in the app. Otherwise, they’re false. Previous review: As my title says, FREE. For now anyway. God help me if they start charging for the basic version. I’d have to go back to NOAA, which is pessimistic and doesn’t do spot forecasts. Mountain Forecast lacks the ability to find ridges or other relatively minor places you might want to hike, but there’s that magic word FREE. And, combined with ACCURATE, it’s pretty much unbeatable. I live close to Rocky Mountain Nat’l Park. I discovered the mountain-forecast site after asking a ranger what they used. I find the app to be significantly more accurate than NOAA, especially because it gives you data on at least two elevations. That’s huge for someone like me who seeks elevation and hates hiking up in the heat. Going down, warm is okay. Also, the app is more accurate on hike day (or morning, as I often do short morning hikes in the foothills). I can see hour-by-hour how it’s going to be, and can get out and enjoy some sun (and often low wind) when I see it’ll cloud up and blow/snow/rain in the afternoon. So, in short, I’m very grateful to the folks behind the app for allowing me easy forecasting accuracy for free. Thank you, mountain forecast.

title: Great app! Very useful info at a glance
body: Have been using the website. Tried the app. It’s well organized, the ‘closest peak’ feature is nice. The graphical display of the freezing line is nice. Would give 5 stars, but the $ for info means I’ll probably go back to using the website. Wife and I only use to check conditions in the summer/fall season.

title: Awesome elevation based temperature
body: Very impressed - preparing for Mt Whitney and having the ability to see what the temperature is not only at the summit, but at the camp ground, completely saved the trip. Apple had the temperature 35° warmer than the altitude feature on mountain forecast - could not be more grateful to prepare appropriately for sub freezing temps. Also the 3D maps are the best I’ve seen.

title: The Best

title: The Final Puzzle Piece
body: Instead of piecing the forecast together from multiple apps and websites Mountain Forecast has been the one stop shop for the most accurate forecasts per mountain. Normally I’d have to make my own predictions based off general location data. Now it’s as easy as looking up your mountaineering subject of choice and bingo everything you will need all in one place. It’s been extremely accurate for me so far. I 100% put trust in Mountain Forecast for my weather info. Perfect for making sure I stay safe and prepared out in the mountains. I highly recommend giving it a try and use it along side your normal weather forecasting process and see what gives you better results and ease of use. For full transparency I pay for the subscription and think it is worth the price, data and ease of use make it a great value. In my opinion you can’t put a price on making it home safely after a trip out into the mountains and accurate forecasts are essential!
